did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 26 opens with a list of the families of the gatekeepers and notes that Meshelemiah son of Kore was a descendant of Korah.
Did you know? Regarding the sons of Obed-Edom, it says, “For God had blessed him.” The passage lists eight sons, from the firstborn, Shemaiah, to the eighth, Peullethai.
Did you know? The sons of Obed-Edom, together with their brothers and sons, are described as capable men qualified for service; their total number was sixty-two.
Did you know? The family connected with Meshelemiah included eighteen capable men—sons and brothers together.
Did you know? Hosa was one of the Merarites, and Shimri was appointed as head even though he was not the firstborn, because his father appointed him to the position.
Did you know? The gatekeepers’ duties were assigned by casting lots, “the small and the great alike,” according to their ancestral families and for each gate.
Did you know? The first lot mentioned fell to the east for Meshelemiah, and to the north for his son Zechariah, who is described as a wise counselor.

Did you know? The gatekeepers were assigned as follows: six Levites to the east, four to the north, four to the south, two at the storehouses, and four to the west at the courtyard, plus two at the road.
Did you know? Shebuel, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was placed in charge of the treasuries—that is, the management of the treasuries of the house of God.

Did you know? Those mentioned in the chapter as having dedicated possessions include Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah; their dedicated gifts were kept in the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
